newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent closes lower in late gasoline-led fall.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent closes lower in late gasoline-led fall.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures moved slightly into the red shortly before the close on Wednesday as a slump on NYMEX gasoline pushed the market off earlier highs.
Dec Brent closed down three cents at $22.16 a barrel, having touched a session high of $22.62.
"(NYMEX) gasoline came off sharply, hitting the stops all the way down, (Brent) just couldn't hold on," said one IPE floor broker.
The move came when traders abandoned their bullish focus on heating oil and concentrated on a bearish build in U.S. gasoline inventories.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures closed 1.11 cents down at 63.50 cents a gallon.

Figures from the American Petroleum Institute (API) showed a 4.7 million barrels increase in gasoline stocks for the week ended Nov 1, while the Energy Information Administration (EIA) estimated a build of 2.7 million barrels.
A draw on distillate stocks had earlier helped support a healthy rally on NYMEX heating oil, which in turn underpinned gains on IPE Brent and gas oil.
The EIA reported that U.S. distillate stocks fell last week by 500,00 barrels, while API figures showed a draw of 429,000 barrels. Analysts had expected a build in stocks of some 2.5 million barrels.
A squeeze on the IPE gas oil front month also appeared to be developing ahead of the contract's expiry on Nov 12.
Nov gas oil closed up $6.25 a tonne at $214.75, with the Nov/Dec backwardation widening by $1.75 on the day to close at $6 a tonne.
"The spreads picked up and finished very strong in the last hour," said one broker.
